the study of weak interactions in the solid state and their role in the modulation of infrared intensities.

the IR intensity of a transition in a molecule in the solid state depends not only on its molecular structure, but also on the dimensionality (1D, 2D, 3D) of the crystal in which it is included.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the IR intensity modulation of the CH2 deformation modes in the solid state can be interpreted as an effect of the local field, and this effect is strongly dependent on the dimensionality and the packing of the units.
we have demonstrated that the intermolecular interaction in the solid state is able to induce a relevant change in the infrared spectrum of a polymeric chain.

the IR spectrum of polyethylene is strongly influenced by the interm molecular packing, as demonstrated by the comparison of calculated spectra for the isolated chain (1D crystal) and for the three dimensional crystal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intermolecular packing plays a crucial role in determining the IR intensity of CH2 deformations in polyethylene.

the intermolecular interactions in the 3D crystal have a strong effect on the computed infrared absorption intensities of the polymer, which is not taken into account in the usual comparison between calculated intensities and experimental data.
the intermolecular interactions in a 3 D crystal can significantly modify the infrared spectrum of a molecule.
